+# Gateway billing and metering: the enforcement/invoicing seam
+
+Status: DESIGN ONLY. Nothing here is implemented or migrated.
+Date: 2026-08-08
+Scope: LLM-gateway spend metering, admission control, and the Stripe seam.
+Related: epic #1579 (billing axis), #1198 / #1289 (metering -> Stripe push, never shipped).
+
+---
+
+## 0. The tension, and why it is not a conflict
+
+Two positions are on the table.
+
+- **Founder decision:** Stripe Billing Meters, Postgres, no ClickHouse.
+- **Draft spec objection:** Stripe processes meter events asynchronously, so
+  usage accrues for a whole cycle before anything is collected. A platform
+  paying for inference up front absorbs that float. The draft therefore
+  proposes a credit ledger with reservations and a synchronous pre-flight
+  returning 402.
+
+These answer **different questions** and both answers are right.
+
+|                                 | Question it answers                   | Latency class         | Authoritative for                                       |
+| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Stripe Billing Meters           | "What does this customer owe?"        | Async, minutes+       | Money owed, invoices, tax, dunning, revenue recognition |
+| Postgres balance + reservations | "May this request proceed right now?" | Synchronous, sub-10ms | Admission control only                                  |
+
+The draft is not arguing against Stripe. It is arguing against using Stripe as
+an **admission oracle**, which Stripe is not built to be and does not claim to
+be. Adopting the credit ledger does not displace Stripe Meters; it supplies the
+thing Meters were never going to supply.
+
+**Verified support for the async claim** (Stripe's own docs, retrieved
+2026-08-08 via the Stripe docs API):
+
+- The Billing Meter Usage Summary / Analytics API "truncates event timestamps
+  to the nearest 15 minutes" -- an event at `08:42:15` is stored at `08:30:00`.
+- It exposes a `data_refreshed_at` field precisely so callers "understand data
+  freshness", and warns to "consider this latency when building real-time
+  dashboards or alerts."
+- That API is in public preview and access-gated by request form.
+
+A system that buckets to 15 minutes, publishes a freshness timestamp, and warns
+you about latency is telling you plainly that it is not a synchronous gate.
+Gating on it would be reading our own lagged aggregate and calling it a
+decision.
+
+### The rule that governs the seam
+
+> **Stripe is authoritative for money owed and is never consulted in the
+> request path. Postgres is authoritative for admission and is never rendered
+> to a customer as an invoice.**
+
+Explicitly forbidden, in both directions:
+
+- **Never** query any Stripe endpoint synchronously to decide whether a request
+  proceeds. Not the meter summary, not the subscription, not entitlements.
+  Stripe's availability must not be in the gateway's request path.
+- **Never** present the Postgres balance as "your bill" or as an amount owed.
+  It is a prepaid/spend-control artefact. Invoices come from Stripe.
+- **Never** treat agreement between the two as a correctness invariant. They
+  will diverge by design (in-flight reservations, unsettled rows, push lag).
+  Divergence is **measured and bounded**, not eliminated. Section 9 is the
+  reconciliation control; without it this whole design has a silent failure
+  mode.
+
+---
+
+## 1. What is actually in the stack today (verified, not assumed)
+
+Every claim below was read out of the repo at commit `e1faeea32`. This matters
+because the brief asked several "is X even in our stack" questions and the
+answers change the design.
+
+### 1.1 Redis IS in the stack. Design with it, but not for money.
+
+The brief asked me to check before designing around it. It is present:
+
+| Evidence                                                 | Location                                                      |
+| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `redis:7-alpine` service + `redis_data` volume           | `docker-compose.production.yml:553-569`                       |
+| Gateway wiring                                           | `docker-compose.production.yml:700` -- `CZ_GATEWAY_REDIS_URL` |
+| Go client dependency                                     | `backend/go.mod` -- `github.com/redis/go-redis/v9 v9.17.2`    |
+| Python client dependency                                 | `gateway/requirements.txt` -- `redis[hiredis]==5.2.1`         |
+| Gateway rate limiter                                     | `gateway/rate_limiter.py:84-95`                               |
+| Backend caches (user, blacklist, org membership, bundle) | `backend/internal/cache/`                                     |
+
+So Redis is available. **This design still puts the balance and reservations in
+Postgres, not Redis.** Redis here is a cache and a rate limiter: it has no
+durability guarantee we are willing to put money behind, and the deployment has
+no replication. Money state needs the same durability as the audit trail.
+Redis keeps its current jobs and gains one new one (Section 7.3, a read-through
+cache of a _hard-denied_ balance, which is a safe thing to cache because it can
+only ever cause a false 402, never a false admit).
+
+### 1.2 The current quota gate has a live read-then-increment race
+
+`backend/internal/api/middleware/usage.go` `CheckLimit`:
+
+```go
+count, err := m.redisClient.Get(r.Context(), key).Int()   // read
+...
+if count >= effectiveLimit { ... }                        // decide
+...
+m.redisClient.Incr(r.Context(), key)                      // then increment
+```
+
+Two concurrent requests at `count == limit-1` both read `limit-1`, both pass the
+predicate, both increment. The gate overshoots by the concurrency level. This is
+exactly the concurrency failure the brief asks the new design to avoid, and it
+is **already shipping** on the actions quota. Section 4 fixes the class.
+
+Two further defects in the same function, worth recording because the new design
+must not inherit them:
+
+- `Incr` failure is fail-open: it logs `"failed to increment usage counter"` and
+  serves the request (`usage.go`, step 5). A Redis that answers `GET` but fails
+  `INCR` grants unmetered quota. The `GET` failure path _is_ correctly
+  fail-closed (429), so the posture is inconsistent between two adjacent lines.
+- The overage counter is `Set` to a value derived from the racy `count`, not
+  `Incr`-ed, so concurrent writers clobber rather than accumulate.
+
+### 1.3 Postgres is not currently a usage system of record
+
+`backend/internal/storage/postgres/admin.go:148` `GetOrganizationUsage`:
+
+```go
+usage := &storage.OrganizationUsage{
+    CurrentMonth: 0, // TODO: Query Redis for usage:{orgID}:{YYYY-MM}
+    ...
+}
+```
+
+It returns a hardcoded zero. `ResetOrganizationUsage` immediately below is a
+documented no-op. The only durable record of usage is a Redis key with a 32-day
+TTL. **There is no usage system of record today.** Any billing built on the
+current state would be billing from a cache.
+
+### 1.4 The existing Stripe usage primitive is the wrong API and has no callers
+
+`backend/internal/billing/stripe.go:702` `CreateUsageRecord` posts to:
+
+```
+/subscription_items/{id}/usage_records
+```
+
+That is the **legacy subscription-item usage records** API, not Billing Meters
+(`/v1/billing/meter_events`). The file's own header comment states it "has NO
+callers yet". So "wire up the existing primitive" is not available: the founder's
+Meters decision needs a **new** client method. Existing tier config that the
+design must respect (`stripe.go`):
+
+| Tier | Actions/month | Over-limit posture      | Planned rate       |
+| ---- | ------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------ |
+| Free | 5,000         | Hard block (429)        | n/a                |
+| Solo | 50,000        | Metered, **not billed** | $10 / 100K actions |
+| Team | 250,000       | Metered, **not billed** | $8 / 100K actions  |
+
+### 1.5 The operator key silently overrides customer BYOK keys
+
+`gateway/proxy.py`, `forward_anthropic`:
+
+```python
+# Gateway-managed key overrides user's key if configured
+if self._settings.anthropic_api_key:
+    forward_headers["x-api-key"] = self._settings.anthropic_api_key
+```
+
+`self._settings.anthropic_api_key` is **global gateway config**, not per-org. If
+an operator key is set, every customer's traffic is billed to it regardless of
+the `x-api-key` the customer sent. There is currently no way for the billing
+layer to know whose money funded a call, because the answer is always "ours"
+whenever that setting is populated.
+
+**This is a precondition, not a detail.** Section 6 (BYOK) is unimplementable
+until key provenance is resolved per-org and recorded on the request. It is also
+a live money leak independent of this design: an org believing it is on BYOK is
+spending the operator's credits today. It should be filed and fixed on its own
+merits.
+
+### 1.6 Token counts are available, and are sometimes absent
+
+`gateway/proxy.py` parses provider usage into `ctx.input_tokens` /
+`ctx.output_tokens` for Anthropic (`message_start` gives input,
+`message_delta` gives output), OpenAI-compatible (`prompt_tokens` /
+`completion_tokens`), Bedrock (`inputTokens` / `outputTokens`), and Vertex/Gemini
+(`promptTokenCount` / `candidatesTokenCount`). All default to `0` via
+`.get(..., 0)`.
+
+Two consequences the design must handle rather than paper over:
+
+- On a stream aborted before the terminal usage event, `output_tokens` stays at
+  its default `0`. **A zero token count is indistinguishable from a missing one**
+  in the current parsing. That is the exact "not run vs ran and found nothing"
+  defect CLAUDE.md rule 5 forbids, and Section 8 is the fix.
+- `input_tokens` arrives early (at `message_start` for Anthropic), so a partial
+  stream usually still yields a trustworthy input count.
+
+### 1.7 ClickHouse: retired, but the package name survives
+
+The service is gone -- `docker-compose.production.yml:576-580` states ClickHouse
+is "fully out of the audit path", the service blocks are commented out, and
+`CLICKHOUSE_URL` was removed 2026-06-11 (epic #1069). Consistent with the founder
+decision.
+
+**Trap for implementers:** the Go package `internal/storage/clickhouse` still
+exists and is imported by `auditmux`, `auditpg`, and `siemexport`. It survives
+only as the home for shared struct definitions (`AuditEvent` and friends). An
+import of that path is not evidence that ClickHouse is back. Do not read it as
+license to reintroduce the datastore, and do not "clean it up" as part of billing
+work.

+## 2. Postgres schema
+
+Migrations 108-110 (current head is 107). Conventions followed:
+
+- Org-scoped tenant tables: `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` + a
+  `FOR ALL USING (org_id = cz_current_org_id()) WITH CHECK (...)` policy, per
+  `094_project_dlp_binding.sql`.
+- Org-agnostic system tables: RLS enabled with **no policy** (deny-all),
+  accessed only via `c.adminQuerier()` with a `// RLS-EXEMPT` annotation, per
+  `074_stripe_webhook_idempotency.sql` and `065_cutover_readiness.sql`.
+- Every `CREATE TABLE` pairs with `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` so
+  `scripts/ci/check-migration-rls.sh` passes on the primary path, not the
+  allowlist escape hatch.
+
+**Money unit:** `BIGINT` micro-dollars (1 USD = 1,000,000). Never float, never
+`NUMERIC` in the hot admission predicate. Micro-dollars because a single
+inference token can cost well under a cent and rounding to cents per request
+loses real revenue at volume; `BIGINT` micro-dollars holds ±9.2 trillion USD,
+which is not a constraint we will meet.
+
+### 2.1 `billing_balances` -- one row per org, the admission authority
+
+```sql
+-- Migration 108: gateway spend balance + reservations.
+
+CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS billing_balances (
+    org_id              UUID PRIMARY KEY
+                        REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+
+    -- Settled funds. Credits added (top-up, plan grant, refund) minus
+    -- settled spend. MAY GO NEGATIVE -- see Section 3.5 on bounded overrun.
+    balance_micros      BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+
+    -- DENORMALISED sum of currently-open reservations. This is NOT a
+    -- convenience column: the atomic admission predicate in Section 4 is only
+    -- correct if it reads a single row. A SUM() over billing_reservations in
+    -- the predicate would defeat Postgres's EvalPlanQual re-check and
+    -- reintroduce the race. billing_reservations is the reconcilable ledger;
+    -- this column is the enforcement value. Section 9 alerts on drift.
+    -- NO CHECK (reserved_micros >= 0). R3: combined with 9.1's "reports,
+    -- never auto-repairs", the obvious CHECK is a self-locking trap. One
+    -- under-statement makes the janitor's batch decrement go negative; the
+    -- CHECK aborts the WHOLE transaction; the next cycle aborts identically;
+    -- self-heal inside the reserve statement hits it too, so the customer gets
+    -- a 500 (not even a 402) on a request they had funds for, forever, until a
+    -- human intervenes. The invariant is enforced by the DRIFT DETECTOR (9.1),
+    -- which observes without blocking. A negative value here is a loud bug,
+    -- not a reason to refuse service -- and it is monitored, not clamped,
+    -- because clamping would be exactly the silent repair 9.1 forbids.
+    reserved_micros     BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+
+    -- Admission floor. Available = balance - reserved; admission requires
+    -- available - cost >= -overdraft_limit_micros. Zero for prepaid orgs;
+    -- positive for invoiced/trusted orgs who may run negative between
+    -- invoices. An explicit, per-org, auditable number -- never a global
+    -- constant and never inferred from tier.
+    overdraft_limit_micros BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
+                        CHECK (overdraft_limit_micros >= 0),
+
+    -- Explicit posture for this org (Section 7). NOT a boolean and NOT
+    -- nullable: an unknown value must be unrepresentable.
+    --   enforce       -> fail closed, 402/503 (default; our key, our money)
+    --   observe_only  -> run the FULL reserve/settle machinery and record what
+    --                    WOULD have happened, but do not deny. See 3.6 --
+    --                    observe_only must never mean "skip the accounting".
+    --   suspended     -> deny all gateway spend regardless of balance
+    enforcement_mode    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'enforce'
+                        CHECK (enforcement_mode IN
+                               ('enforce', 'observe_only', 'suspended')),
+
+    -- HARD ceiling for observe_only orgs (3.6). observe_only does not deny on
+    -- balance, so without this it is an UNBOUNDED operator-spend exposure.
+    -- NULL is only valid when enforcement_mode <> 'observe_only'.
+    observe_ceiling_micros BIGINT
+                        CHECK (observe_ceiling_micros IS NULL
+                               OR observe_ceiling_micros >= 0),
+
+    CONSTRAINT billing_balances_observe_needs_ceiling
+        CHECK (enforcement_mode <> 'observe_only'
+               OR observe_ceiling_micros IS NOT NULL),
+
+    currency            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'usd',
+    updated_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
+    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
+);
+
+ALTER TABLE billing_balances ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+
+CREATE POLICY billing_balances_tenant_isolation ON billing_balances FOR ALL
+    USING (org_id = cz_current_org_id())
+    WITH CHECK (org_id = cz_current_org_id());
+
+COMMENT ON TABLE billing_balances IS
+    'Gateway spend admission authority (one row per org). Authoritative for '
+    '"may this request proceed", NEVER for "what does the customer owe" -- '
+    'invoices come from Stripe. reserved_micros is denormalised so the '
+    'admission predicate reads a single row (see migration comment).';
+```
+
+### 2.2 `billing_reservations` -- in-flight holds
+
+```sql
+CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS billing_reservations (
+    id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
+    org_id              UUID NOT NULL
+                        REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+
+    -- Worst-case cost held against the balance (Section 3.4).
+    amount_micros       BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (amount_micros >= 0),
+
+    -- open -> settled | released | expired. Terminal states are final:
+    -- the settle/release statements assert state='open' in their WHERE
+    -- clause, so a duplicate settle is a no-op rather than a double charge.
+    state               TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open'
+                        CHECK (state IN ('open','settled','released','expired')),
+
+    -- Reclaim deadline. Set to provider timeout + margin at reserve time.
+    -- The janitor AND the org's own next reserve both sweep on this.
+    expires_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
+
+    -- Correlates to the gateway request; also the settle idempotency anchor.
+    request_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
+    model               TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
+    provider            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
+
+    -- Who funds this call. Decides whether a reservation exists at all
+    -- (Section 6). Closed vocabulary, no default -- an unrecognised key
+    -- source must fail loudly at insert, not fall through.
+    key_source          TEXT NOT NULL
+                        CHECK (key_source IN ('operator','customer_byok')),
+
+    -- Why the reservation left 'open'. Distinguishes a normal settle from a
+    -- janitor sweep from a client disconnect. Never NULL once terminal.
+    close_reason        TEXT
+    -- R3 finding 16b: 'released_quota_denied' is NOT optional. Under a
+    -- gate-B-then-gate-A ordering the spend hold must be released because the
+    -- ACTIONS quota refused. With no member for it, an implementer picks the
+    -- nearest permitted value -- almost certainly 'released_policy_denied' --
+    -- and the policy-denial rate in the audit record becomes unreliable. A
+    -- closed vocabulary missing a real member does not fail loudly; it pushes
+    -- the caller into mislabelling.
+                        CHECK (close_reason IS NULL OR close_reason IN
+                               ('settled_exact','settled_reserved_fallback',
+                                'settled_partial','released_provider_error',
+                                'released_timeout','released_client_disconnect',
+                                'released_policy_denied','released_quota_denied',
+                                'expired_janitor','expired_self_heal')),
+
+    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
+    closed_at           TIMESTAMPTZ
+);
+
+ALTER TABLE billing_reservations ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+
+CREATE POLICY billing_reservations_tenant_isolation ON billing_reservations
+    FOR ALL
+    USING (org_id = cz_current_org_id())
+    WITH CHECK (org_id = cz_current_org_id());
+
+-- The reclaim sweep. Partial index keeps it proportional to open holds,
+-- not to history.
+CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_billing_reservations_open_expiry
+    ON billing_reservations (org_id, expires_at)
+    WHERE state = 'open';
+
+-- One reservation per gateway request. This is the structural guard against
+-- a retried reserve double-holding funds (Section 3.2).
+CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_billing_reservations_request
+    ON billing_reservations (org_id, request_id);
+```
+
+### 2.3 `billing_usage` -- settled rows, the usage system of record
+
+Monthly `RANGE` partitions on `occurred_at` (Section 10 has the volume math).
+
+```sql
+CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS billing_usage (
+    id                  UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
+    org_id              UUID NOT NULL,
+    reservation_id      UUID,          -- NULL for BYOK (no reservation taken)
+    request_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
+    occurred_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
+
+    provider            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
+    model               TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
+    key_source          TEXT NOT NULL
+                        CHECK (key_source IN ('operator','customer_byok')),
+
+    input_tokens        BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+    output_tokens       BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+
+    -- What we charged the balance. 0 for BYOK, and 0 is MEANINGFUL only in
+    -- combination with metering_state below.
+    cost_micros         BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+
+    -- Amount by which actual exceeded the hold. Bounded exposure metric
+    -- (Section 3.5); alerting reads this.
+    overrun_micros      BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+
+    -- ---- CLAUDE.md rule 5: "not run" must differ from "ran, found nothing" ----
+    --
+    -- metering_state answers "did spend metering run for this request?"
+    --   metered                    -> ran, cost_micros is a measurement
+    --   not_applicable_byok        -> deliberately not metered; customer's key
+    --   skipped_observe_only       -> gate in observe mode; recorded, not charged
+    --   unavailable_storage_down   -> could NOT run; cost unknown, not zero
+    --   errored                    -> ran and failed; cost unknown
+    -- A zero cost_micros with 'metered' means genuinely free.
+    -- A zero cost_micros with 'unavailable_storage_down' means we do not know.
+    -- These must never collapse into the same row shape.
+    --   denied_admission           -> refused before any provider call; no cost
+    --                                 incurred, but the ACTION was consumed and
+    --                                 must still be recorded (R3 finding 16a:
+    --                                 without this, an all-denied period looks
+    --                                 identical to a dead gateway, and a
+    --                                 customer asking "why 4,000 402s" has only
+    --                                 a Prometheus counter, not a record).
+    --   released_no_tokens         -> provider call attempted, nothing generated
+    metering_state      TEXT NOT NULL
+                        CHECK (metering_state IN
+                               ('metered','not_applicable_byok',
+                                'skipped_observe_only',
+                                'denied_admission','released_no_tokens',
+                                'unavailable_storage_down','errored')),
+
+    -- Governed-action count. 1 for every request that reached policy
+    -- evaluation, whatever the outcome -- INCLUDING denials and releases
+    -- (6.4). This is the quantity cz_governed_actions meters and the basis of
+    -- the BYOK tier.
+    actions             SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (actions >= 0),
+
+    -- Soak output: TRUE when observe_only admitted something enforce would
+    -- have refused (3.6). NULL for orgs not in observe mode.
+    would_have_denied   BOOLEAN,
+
+    -- token_source answers "where did the token numbers come from?"
+    --   provider_reported -> the provider's terminal usage block. Trustworthy.
+    --   partial_stream    -> input known, output truncated by disconnect.
+    --   reserved_fallback -> provider reported nothing; billed the hold
+    --                        under the disclosed policy (Section 7.4).
+    --   absent            -> no counts at all and no fallback applied.
+    -- 'absent' with output_tokens = 0 is NOT the same fact as
+    -- 'provider_reported' with output_tokens = 0.
+    token_source        TEXT NOT NULL
+                        CHECK (token_source IN
+                               ('provider_reported','partial_stream',
+                                'reserved_fallback','absent')),
+
+    -- NO push state here. An earlier draft carried pushed_at / push_attempts /
+    -- push_last_error / meter_event_id on this table; reviewer R3 showed a
+    -- single flag cannot represent a three-meter fan-out, starves the pusher
+    -- on permanently-unpushable rows, and makes quarantine unimplementable.
+    -- Push state is per (row, meter) in billing_meter_pushes (5.5).
+
+    PRIMARY KEY (id, occurred_at)
+) PARTITION BY RANGE (occurred_at);
+
+ALTER TABLE billing_usage ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+
+CREATE POLICY billing_usage_tenant_isolation ON billing_usage FOR ALL
+    USING (org_id = cz_current_org_id())
+    WITH CHECK (org_id = cz_current_org_id());
+
+-- Idempotency of settlement itself.
+CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_billing_usage_request
+    ON billing_usage (org_id, request_id, occurred_at);
+
+-- The pusher's work queue lives on billing_meter_pushes (5.5), not here.
+
+-- Rollup source scan: one partition, one day, grouped.
+CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_billing_usage_org_time
+    ON billing_usage (org_id, occurred_at);
+```
+
+RLS on a partitioned parent propagates to partitions in Postgres 17 (prod is
+17.10), but the CI guard scans `CREATE TABLE` text, so **each partition
+creation must carry its own `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`**. The partition-creation
+job must emit it, or the guard fires on the first monthly roll -- correctly.
+
+### 2.4 `billing_usage_daily` -- rollup that dashboards read
+
+```sql
+CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS billing_usage_daily (
+    org_id          UUID NOT NULL,
+    day             DATE NOT NULL,
+    provider        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
+    model           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
+    key_source      TEXT NOT NULL,
+    metering_state  TEXT NOT NULL,     -- carried, NOT summed away
+    -- R3 finding 16d: token_source must be in the key too. It is the
+    -- OVER-BILLING signal (7.4: "if reserved_fallback climbs ... we are
+    -- over-billing at scale"), and Section 10's 100-day retention drops the raw
+    -- partitions. Summed away here, the fallback rate for any period older than
+    -- 100 days is unrecoverable from anything that survives -- exactly the
+    -- aggregation dishonesty this table added metering_state to prevent.
+    token_source    TEXT NOT NULL,
+
+    requests        BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+    actions         BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+    input_tokens    BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+    output_tokens   BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+    cost_micros     BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+
+    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
+    PRIMARY KEY (org_id, day, provider, model, key_source,
+                 metering_state, token_source)
+);
+
+ALTER TABLE billing_usage_daily ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+
+CREATE POLICY billing_usage_daily_tenant_isolation ON billing_usage_daily
+    FOR ALL
+    USING (org_id = cz_current_org_id())
+    WITH CHECK (org_id = cz_current_org_id());
+```
+
+`metering_state` is in the primary key deliberately. If it were summed away, a
+day where half the requests were `unavailable_storage_down` would render as a
+confident low number, and the dashboard would be lying by aggregation. Keeping
+it in the key means an incomplete day is _visibly_ incomplete.
+
+### 2.5 `billing_balance_entries` -- append-only ledger behind the balance
+
+`billing_balances.balance_micros` is a single mutable number. On its own it
+cannot answer _"why is my balance this?"_, and a governance product that cannot
+explain its own money movements has no standing to ask customers to trust its
+audit trail. `billing_usage` records every **debit**, but credits (top-ups, plan
+grants, refunds, admin adjustments) would have no record at all.
+
+```sql
+CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS billing_balance_entries (
+    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
+    org_id          UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+
+    -- Signed. Positive = credit, negative = debit.
+    delta_micros    BIGINT NOT NULL,
+
+    -- Closed vocabulary. A new money-movement reason must be added here
+    -- deliberately; it cannot arrive as free text.
+    reason          TEXT NOT NULL
+                    CHECK (reason IN ('topup_stripe','plan_grant','refund',
+                                      'admin_adjustment','usage_settlement',
+                                      'overrun_writeoff','migration_opening')),
+
+    -- Provenance. Exactly one is non-NULL for machine-generated entries;
+    -- admin_adjustment carries actor_user_id and a mandatory note.
+    usage_id        UUID,
+    stripe_object_id TEXT,
+    actor_user_id   UUID,
+    note            TEXT,
+
+    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
+
+    CONSTRAINT billing_balance_entries_admin_needs_actor
+        CHECK (reason <> 'admin_adjustment'
+               OR (actor_user_id IS NOT NULL AND note IS NOT NULL))
+);
+
+ALTER TABLE billing_balance_entries ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+
+CREATE POLICY billing_balance_entries_tenant_isolation
+    ON billing_balance_entries FOR ALL
+    USING (org_id = cz_current_org_id())
+    WITH CHECK (org_id = cz_current_org_id());
+
+CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_billing_balance_entries_org_time
+    ON billing_balance_entries (org_id, created_at DESC);
+```
+
+Every write that moves `balance_micros` writes an entry **in the same
+transaction**. This yields a second drift check alongside 9.1:
+
+```sql
+SELECT b.org_id, b.balance_micros, COALESCE(SUM(e.delta_micros), 0) AS ledger
+  FROM billing_balances b
+  LEFT JOIN billing_balance_entries e ON e.org_id = b.org_id
+ GROUP BY b.org_id, b.balance_micros
+HAVING b.balance_micros <> COALESCE(SUM(e.delta_micros), 0);
+```
+
+Deliberately **append-only**: no `UPDATE`, no `DELETE`. A correction is a new
+compensating entry, never an edit. Revoke `UPDATE`/`DELETE` on this table from
+the application role so the property is enforced by the database rather than by
+convention.
+
+Note that `usage_settlement` entries duplicate information already in
+`billing_usage`. That redundancy is intentional: it lets the balance be
+reconstructed from one append-only table without joining the partitioned usage
+history, including for periods whose raw partitions have been dropped under the
+retention policy in Section 10.
+
+### 2.6 Pricing: record the price, do not look it up later
+
+A settled row that stores only token counts cannot reproduce its own charge once
+model prices change. Six months later, a customer disputing an invoice gets an
+answer computed with today's prices against last year's tokens, and we would
+have no way to tell whether we were right.
+
+The unit prices used are therefore **recorded on the row**:
+
+```sql
+ALTER TABLE billing_usage
+    ADD COLUMN price_in_micros_per_mtok  BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+    ADD COLUMN price_out_micros_per_mtok BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+    ADD COLUMN price_version             TEXT   NOT NULL DEFAULT '';
+```
+
+Per _million_ tokens, because per-token micro-dollar prices round to zero for
+cheap models -- a real precision bug rather than a stylistic choice.
+`cost_micros` is then always reproducible from the row alone:
+
+```
+cost_micros = round(input_tokens  * price_in_micros_per_mtok  / 1_000_000)
+            + round(output_tokens * price_out_micros_per_mtok / 1_000_000)
+```
+
+`price_version` identifies the price table generation, so a mispriced model can
+be found and corrected in bulk with an exact blast radius.
+
+**Unknown model:** a model absent from the price table is a **fail-closed**
+admission denial for operator-key traffic (we cannot bound the cost of something
+we cannot price), and a normal `not_applicable_byok` record for BYOK. It is
+never priced at zero -- pricing an unknown at zero is precisely the
+silent-success shape where a broken price table looks like a free month. Add it
+to the failure-posture table as row 26.
+
+**Currency:** USD only. The `currency` column exists so a future multi-currency
+change is a migration rather than a redesign; until then a non-`usd` value is
+rejected, not converted.
+
+### 2.7 `billing_meter_push_watermark` -- lease + lag observability
+
+The brief asked for a watermark. It is here, but **it is not the correctness
+mechanism** -- see Section 5.2 for why a sequence cursor would silently skip
+rows. This table holds the single-pusher lease (the migration-074 pattern) and
+the observable lag.
+
+```sql
+CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS billing_meter_push_watermark (
+    meter_name          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+
+    -- Lease: exactly one pusher at a time. Same shape as
+    -- stripe_webhook_events (#1217): authorise on lock_token ownership,
+    -- steal only when locked_until < now().
+    lock_token          UUID,
+    locked_until        TIMESTAMPTZ,
+
+    -- OBSERVABILITY, not correctness. Derived from the unpushed set each
+    -- cycle; alerting reads these.
+    oldest_unpushed_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
+    unpushed_rows       BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+    last_success_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
+    last_error          TEXT,
+
+    -- Distinguishes "never ran" from "ran, nothing to push" (rule 5 again).
+    --   never_run | idle_no_work | pushing | degraded_stripe_error
+    push_state          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'never_run'
+                        CHECK (push_state IN
+                               ('never_run','idle_no_work','pushing',
+                                'degraded_stripe_error')),
+
+    updated_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
+);
+
+-- Org-agnostic system/infra table: RLS-enabled, NO policy = deny-all.
+-- Touched only by the BYPASSRLS admin pool (c.adminQuerier(), // RLS-EXEMPT).
+-- Matches the 074 / 065 convention.
+ALTER TABLE billing_meter_push_watermark ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+```

+## 3. The reservation state machine
+
+```
+                        ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
+                        │  admission (Section 4)          │
+                        │  atomic conditional UPDATE      │
+                        └───────────┬─────────────────────┘
+                    insufficient    │    sufficient
+                         │          │
+                         ▼          ▼
+                   402 no hold    OPEN ──────────────────────┐
+                                    │                         │
+        ┌───────────────────────────┼─────────────┬───────────┤
+        │ provider returned usage   │ error/      │ no usage  │ nobody
+        │                           │ timeout/    │ reported  │ closed it
+        ▼                           ▼ disconnect  ▼           ▼
+     SETTLED                     RELEASED      SETTLED      EXPIRED
+  close_reason=                close_reason=  close_reason= close_reason=
+  settled_exact                released_*     settled_      expired_janitor
+  | settled_partial                           reserved_     | expired_
+                                              fallback      self_heal
+        │                           │             │           │
+        └───────────────────────────┴─────────────┴───────────┘
+                                    │
+                            reserved_micros released
+                            balance debited by actual (settle only)
+```
+
+### 3.1 Reserve
+
+**One statement, and the reservation `INSERT` must be inside it.** Reviewer R1
+found that an earlier draft described this while showing only the balance
+`UPDATE` in Section 4 -- an implementer following the SQL literally would split
+the two, and a crash between them leaves `reserved_micros` inflated with no
+matching open reservation. The customer's available balance is then permanently
+understated and they get 402s they have not earned, until an operator notices
+the drift alert. The full statement is in Section 4 and includes the `INSERT`.
+
+### 3.2 Reserve is idempotent on `request_id`
+
+`idx_billing_reservations_request` is `UNIQUE (org_id, request_id)`. A retried
+reserve for the same gateway request hits the conflict and returns the existing
+hold rather than taking a second one. Without this, a client retry storm against
+a near-empty balance holds the balance N times over and 402s a customer who has
+funds -- a self-inflicted denial of service on a paying account.
+
+### 3.3 Settle
+
+The naive form -- one statement guarded on `state = 'open'` -- has a money-loss
+hole, found in self-review before the external reviews and recorded here because
+it is the least obvious part of the design:
+
+> A generation legitimately outlives `expires_at`. The janitor expires the hold
+> and releases `reserved_micros`. The call then completes normally and settle
+> arrives. `WHERE state = 'open'` does not match, settle is a no-op, and **we
+> never charge for inference we actually paid for.** No error is raised
+> anywhere; the request looks perfectly successful.
+
+`expired` is therefore a _settleable_ state with different arithmetic, not a
+terminal one. Only `settled` and `released` are terminal.
+
+There is a second hole, and it is the most expensive defect either reviewer
+found. Reviewer R1: if the `billing_usage` insert is a **separate statement**
+from the balance debit, a crash between them leaves the balance debited with no
+usage row. The Stripe pusher scans `billing_usage`, so that request is
+**invisible to invoicing forever** -- we charged the internal balance and billed
+the customer nothing. On a postpaid org that is pure revenue loss with no error
+raised anywhere.
+
+Settle is therefore **one statement with four effects**: close the reservation,
+debit the balance, write the usage row, write the ledger entry.
+
+> **PG 17 trap, found by reviewer R3 and load-bearing.** An earlier draft wrote
+> `RETURNING amount_micros, state AS prior_state` on the closing `UPDATE`.
+> Postgres `RETURNING` yields the **post-update** value; `OLD.`/`NEW.` aliases in
+> `RETURNING` arrived in **PostgreSQL 18**, and prod is **17.10**. So
+> `prior_state` was always the literal `'settled'`, the `CASE` below never took
+> its `'open'` branch, and `reserved_micros` was **never released on any
+> settle**. Every org's holds would accumulate monotonically until the admission
+> predicate failed permanently -- a 402 storm against customers with money,
+> repairable only by hand because 9.1 refuses to auto-repair. The prior state
+> must be captured in a **preceding** CTE that locks the row.
+
+```sql
+WITH prior AS (
+    -- Capture pre-update state under a row lock. This CTE, not RETURNING,
+    -- is what makes prior_state trustworthy on PG 17.
+    SELECT id, amount_micros, state AS prior_state
+      FROM billing_reservations
+     WHERE id = $1 AND org_id = $2
+       AND state IN ('open', 'expired')      -- NOT 'open' alone
+       FOR UPDATE
+), closed AS (
+    UPDATE billing_reservations r
+       SET state = 'settled',
+           close_reason = $3,
+           closed_at = now()
+      FROM prior
+     WHERE r.id = prior.id
+    RETURNING prior.amount_micros, prior.prior_state
+), debited AS (
+    UPDATE billing_balances b
+       SET balance_micros  = b.balance_micros - $4,   -- actual cost, always
+           -- Release the hold ONLY if it was still open. An expired hold was
+           -- already released by the janitor; subtracting again would credit
+           -- the org twice and drive reserved_micros negative.
+           reserved_micros = b.reserved_micros
+                           - CASE WHEN closed.prior_state = 'open'
+                                  THEN closed.amount_micros ELSE 0 END,
+           updated_at = now()
+      FROM closed
+     WHERE b.org_id = $2
+    RETURNING b.org_id, b.balance_micros
+), usage AS (
+    INSERT INTO billing_usage
+        (org_id, reservation_id, request_id, occurred_at, provider, model,
+         key_source, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_micros, overrun_micros,
+         metering_state, token_source, meter_event_id,
+         price_in_micros_per_mtok, price_out_micros_per_mtok, price_version)
+    SELECT debited.org_id, $1, $5, $6, $7, $8, $9, $10, $11, $4,
+           GREATEST(0, $4 - closed.amount_micros),
+           $12, $13, $14, $15, $16, $17
+      FROM debited, closed
+    ON CONFLICT (org_id, request_id, occurred_at) DO NOTHING
+    RETURNING id, org_id
+)
+INSERT INTO billing_balance_entries (org_id, delta_micros, reason, usage_id)
+SELECT usage.org_id, -$4, 'usage_settlement', usage.id FROM usage
+RETURNING id;
+```
+
+All four effects commit together or none do. A crash at any point leaves the
+reservation `open`, which the sweep reclaims and which leaves the request
+**unbilled but also uncharged** -- a consistent state that the reconciliation in
+9.1 can detect, rather than the silent asymmetry of a debit with no invoice.
+
+`ON CONFLICT (org_id, request_id, occurred_at) DO NOTHING` on `billing_usage`
+makes the settle idempotent at the usage layer as well as the reservation layer
+-- **but only if `occurred_at` is byte-identical across replays**, and reviewer
+R3 found that nothing in an earlier draft required that.
+
+`occurred_at` is a bind parameter. If the spool replayer stamps `now()` at
+replay time -- the natural implementation -- every attempt gets a different
+value, `ON CONFLICT` never fires, and a crash between the insert commit and the
+spool-entry delete produces a **second usage row for one request**, with its own
+`id`, its own `meter_event_id`, and therefore its own un-deduplicated Stripe
+event. The customer is billed twice.
+
+**Rule: `occurred_at` is stamped ONCE, at the moment the provider response
+completes, and is carried verbatim through the spool file and every replay.** It
+is request data, not a write timestamp. Use `created_at DEFAULT now()` for "when
+was this row written"; the two must never be conflated.
+
+**And the BYOK path needs its own idempotent writer.** 6.2 is explicit that BYOK
+takes no reservation at all, so the settle statement above -- driven entirely by
+the `closed` CTE -- is not the statement that writes BYOK rows, and the
+`state IN ('open','expired')` guard that provides double-charge protection does
+not exist for that population. The BYOK usage insert is a separate statement
+whose only protection is the `(org_id, request_id, occurred_at)` unique index,
+which makes the stamped-once rule above load-bearing for every BYOK customer
+rather than an edge case.
+
+The balance is debited in **both** cases -- the inference happened and was paid
+for -- while the hold is released only if it was still held. A late settle
+against an expired hold therefore charges correctly and may push the balance
+negative, which is the bounded-overrun case (3.5) and is preferable to silently
+absorbing the cost.
+
+Zero rows returned now means genuinely terminal (already `settled` or
+`released`). That is a **no-op, not an error**: the duplicate settle did
+nothing, which is correct. The caller records `settlement_duplicate_total` so a
+retry storm is visible rather than silent.
+
+The `state IN ('open','expired')` predicate is the double-charge guard, and the
+`CASE` is the double-release guard. Both are properties of the statement, not of
+the caller's discipline.
+
+**Corollary on `expires_at`:** it must exceed the maximum provider timeout by a
+wide margin. Its job is reclaiming holds from _dead_ requests, not from slow
+ones. Set it to `provider_timeout × 2` at minimum, and alert if the
+`expired_janitor` -> late-settle rate is anything but near-zero -- that pattern
+means the TTL is too tight and customers are being charged against a
+released hold more often than they should be.
+
+### 3.4 Reserve the worst case, not an estimate
+
+```
+reserve_micros = ceil(
+      known_input_tokens  * price_in_micros_per_token(model)
+    + max_tokens          * price_out_micros_per_token(model)
+) capped at reserve_cap_micros
+```
+
+`max_tokens` comes from the request body, which the gateway already parses
+(`_parse_anthropic_request`). If the caller omits it, use the model's documented
+maximum -- **never a guessed average**.
+
+Reserving the worst case makes overrun structurally near-zero: actual output can
+never exceed `max_tokens`, so the hold covers the call. The cost is a real UX
+regression: an org with $1 available sending `max_tokens=64000` gets a 402 for a
+call that would have cost $0.02.
+
+`reserve_cap_micros` is the escape valve, and it is an **explicit trade**, not a
+free lunch: capping the hold below worst case reintroduces overrun exactly
+equal to the gap. State the exposure rather than hiding it (Section 3.5).
+
+### 3.5 Overrun is permitted, bounded, and measured
+
+If actual exceeds the hold, the settle debits the actual amount and the balance
+may go negative. We cannot un-spend inference that already happened; refusing to
+record it would make the ledger wrong in our own favour, which is the same class
+of error as over-claiming.
+
+Negative balance blocks the _next_ request (the predicate in Section 4 fails).
+
+**The exposure formula in an earlier draft was wrong, and reviewer R3 showed it
+wrong in three independent ways.** It read:
+
+```
+max_exposure = max_concurrent x max(0, worst_case_cost - reserve_cap_micros)   -- WRONG
+```
+
+which implied "uncapped means zero exposure". That conclusion is false:
+
+**(a) `known_input_tokens` is not known at reserve time.** Section 1.6
+establishes that input counts arrive in the _provider's response_
+(`message_start` for Anthropic). Before the call the gateway has `max_tokens`
+from the request body but only an _estimate_ of input. Prompt caching, tool
+definitions, system prompts and a 200K context all price on input, so the
+estimate can be short by a large multiple. A request estimated at 2K input
+tokens but actually carrying 190K, on a model at $3/Mtok input, holds $0.006 of
+input cost against $0.57 incurred -- with no cap involved anywhere.
+
+**(b) An expired-but-live hold frees capacity for inference still running and
+still unpaid.** 3.3 and row 28 make this normal and expected. A provider
+slowdown pushes 100 in-flight holds past `expires_at`; the janitor releases all
+100; the balance returns to full and admits 100 more. Now 200 are in flight, 100
+backed by no hold at all, each exposed at the **full** worst case.
+
+**(c) `max_concurrent_requests_per_org` is bounded by nothing.** `rate_limiter.py`
+limits _rate_, not concurrency. With a cap set, concurrency is implicitly bounded
+by `available / cap` -- so a well-funded org's exposure grows with its own
+top-up, which is not what the formula communicated.
+
+Corrected, the bound is at minimum:
+
+```
+max_exposure >= overdraft_limit_micros
+              + (concurrent_admitted    x max(0, worst_case - reserve_cap))
+              + (expired_but_live_holds x worst_case_cost)
+              + SUM(input_estimate_error x price_in)
+```
+
+No term is zero by default, and the third is driven by provider latency rather
+than by anything we control. Required mitigations, none optional:
+
+- **A hard per-org concurrency cap** on operator-funded requests. Without it the
+  first factor is unbounded and the formula has no value.
+- **`expires_at` >= 2x max provider timeout** (3.3), so term three stays near
+  zero in normal operation, plus an alert on the expired-then-late-settle rate.
+- **Reserve input at a defensible upper bound**, never a client-supplied guess --
+  e.g. payload-bytes / min-chars-per-token, which over-estimates by construction.
+- Record `overrun_micros` per row and alert on the org-level sum. The formula is
+  a design aid; this metric is the evidence that the bound holds in reality.
+
+Section 12's "launch uncapped" recommendation is **withdrawn** on this basis.
+
+### 3.6 `observe_only` must observe, not abstain
+
+Reviewer R2's sharpest finding, and it changes the semantics of the mode.
+
+An earlier draft had `observe_only` **bypass** the reserve/settle path entirely:
+admit, record `metering_state='skipped_observe_only'`, move on. Two consequences,
+both bad:
+
+**It observes nothing.** The entire point of a soak is to learn what enforcement
+_would_ have done -- how many requests would have been denied, for which orgs, at
+what balance. A mode that skips the machinery produces none of that. It is not
+an observation mode; it is an off switch with a reassuring name. When the soak
+ends and enforcement is switched on, the first real data arrives in production.
+
+**It is an unbounded spend exposure.** The bounded-overrun formula in 3.5 assumes
+every operator-funded call takes a hold. Under bypass there is no hold, no cap,
+and no `reserve_cap_micros`. Concretely:
+
+1. New customer onboarded, set `observe_only` for a 30-day soak.
+2. They run 10M tokens/day on the **operator's** key. No reservation, no debit.
+3. Stripe invoices them; they dispute or churn without paying.
+4. Dunning exhausts, the org is suspended -- **after** we have paid the provider
+   for 300M tokens with zero tracked exposure and no point at which anything
+   would have stopped.
+
+The formula in 3.5 evaluates to zero for BYOK and zero for uncapped enforce, and
+was simply **undefined** for this case. An exposure the model does not represent
+is not a small exposure; it is an unmeasured one.
+
+**Corrected semantics:**
+
+- `observe_only` runs the **full** reserve/settle path: hold taken, balance
+  debited, usage row written, ledger entry written.
+- The only difference is that a failed admission predicate **does not deny**. It
+  records `would_have_denied = true` on the usage row and serves the request.
+  That field is the soak's actual output.
+- `metering_state` becomes `metered` (the accounting genuinely ran).
+  `skipped_observe_only` is retained in the vocabulary only for the narrow case
+  where the machinery itself could not run, and is no longer the normal
+  observe-mode value.
+- A **hard ceiling** (`observe_ceiling_micros`, 2.1) bounds cumulative
+  observe-mode spend per org. Reaching it denies regardless of mode, and pages.
+  The `CHECK` constraint makes an `observe_only` org without a ceiling
+  **unrepresentable** -- the exposure cannot be created by forgetting a field.
+
+The general lesson, which is the same one CLAUDE.md draws about controls gating
+on borrowed predicates: a mode that turns off enforcement must not also turn off
+_measurement_, or the thing you are soaking produces no evidence and the soak
+cannot end on data.
+
+### 3.7 Every way a reservation can leak, and how it is reclaimed
+
+A hold that never closes silently throttles a paying customer. Enumerated:
+
+| #   | Leak                                                                                                    | Reclaim                                                                                                                                                     |
+| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| 1   | Gateway process crashes between reserve and settle                                                      | `expires_at` sweep (janitor + self-heal)                                                                                                                    |
+| 2   | Gateway pod SIGKILL / OOM -- no cleanup code runs at all                                                | Same. This is why reclaim cannot live in a `finally` block alone                                                                                            |
+| 3   | Client disconnects mid-stream                                                                           | Explicit release on the disconnect path; sweep is the backstop                                                                                              |
+| 4   | Provider timeout (`httpx.TimeoutException` -> 504)                                                      | Explicit release, `released_timeout`                                                                                                                        |
+| 5   | Provider connect error (`httpx.ConnectError` -> 502)                                                    | Explicit release, `released_provider_error`                                                                                                                 |
+| 6   | Unhandled exception (the bare `except Exception` in `forward_anthropic`)                                | Explicit release in that handler; sweep is the backstop                                                                                                     |
+| 7   | Postgres connection lost after reserve, before settle                                                   | Sweep. Settle cannot be written, so nothing else can work                                                                                                   |
+| 8   | Settle partially applied (reservation closed, balance update lost)                                      | Impossible -- both are one statement in one transaction                                                                                                     |
+| 9   | Duplicate settle                                                                                        | No-op via `WHERE state='open'` (3.3)                                                                                                                        |
+| 10  | Reserve retried by the client                                                                           | No-op via `UNIQUE (org_id, request_id)` (3.2)                                                                                                               |
+| 11  | Clock skew makes `expires_at` never arrive                                                              | `expires_at` is computed `now() + interval` **in Postgres**, never from gateway wall clock. Single clock, no skew                                           |
+| 12  | Org deleted mid-flight                                                                                  | `ON DELETE CASCADE` removes holds with the org                                                                                                              |
+| 13  | Janitor itself dies                                                                                     | Self-heal (3.7) covers the customer-visible symptom; the janitor's own liveness is alerted separately                                                       |
+| 14  | Janitor expires a hold for a request that is **still live**; settle then finds no open hold             | **This is money loss, not a leak.** Settle accepts `expired` and debits anyway (3.3). `expires_at` must exceed max provider timeout by 2x                   |
+| 15  | Self-heal and janitor touch the same rows concurrently -> deadlock, reserve aborts, customer sees a 500 | Fixed lock order everywhere: `billing_reservations` first, then `billing_balances`. Janitor uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` so it never blocks a live reserve |
+
+**Two independent reclaim paths, deliberately:**
+
+1. **Self-heal on the org's own next reserve.** Before evaluating the predicate,
+   the reserve transaction expires that org's overdue holds. A leak therefore
+   costs a customer at most `expires_at` worth of throttling, and heals on their
+   next request without any background process being alive. This removes the
+   janitor from the customer-facing failure path.
+2. **Background janitor**, every 60s, all orgs. Catches holds for orgs that have
+   gone quiet -- exactly the case self-heal cannot reach, since it needs a next
+   request to trigger.
+
+Neither is sufficient alone, and the two fail for different reasons, which is
+the point.
+
+**If reclaim silently stopped working, what would look different?**
+`billing_reservation_open_age_seconds` (max age of any open hold) would climb
+past `expires_at` and stay there. Alert on that, not on the janitor's exit code
+-- a janitor that runs successfully and sweeps nothing because of a predicate
+bug exits 0. The age metric measures the _effect_; the exit code measures our
+own report of ourselves.
+
